items.prompt:
Weathering is
A) moving rock pieces
B) breaking rock into smaller pieces
C) making new rock only
D) growing plants
items.answer: B) breaking rock into smaller pieces

steps: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces.

items.prompt:
Erosion is
A) breaking rock
B) moving rock pieces from place to place
C) freezing water
D) planting trees
items.answer: B) moving rock pieces from place to place

items.prompt:
Which can cause erosion?
A) Water
B) A drawing
C) A color
D) Silence

steps: Water, ice, wind, and plants cause erosion.

items.prompt:
Water freezing in a crack and splitting a rock is
A) erosion
B) weathering
C) neither
D) a fossil

steps: Breaking the rock apart is weathering.

items.prompt:
A river carrying sand downstream is an example of
A) weathering
B) erosion
C) freezing
D) growing

Water erodes sand faster on
A) flat ground
B) a steep slope
C) no slope at all
D) dry ground

steps: Faster water on a steep slope erodes more.

items.prompt:
To fairly compare erosion by water and wind, you should
A) use different sand each time
B) use identical sand piles and apply equal water and wind for the same time
C) change many things at once
D) not measure anything
items.answer: B) use identical sand piles and apply equal water and wind for the same time

steps: Keeping everything equal except the force makes it fair.

items.prompt:
A grassy hillside loses less soil in a storm than a bare one because plant roots
A) make more rain
B) hold the soil in place
C) speed up the water
D) have no effect
items.answer: B) hold the soil in place

steps: Roots anchor the soil, reducing erosion.
